clue.text: " The child is father…"? But the reverse describes the recess

indicators.note: the clue tells us to read the quoted phrase's pieces from the back to the front

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a child
pa is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: A line of Wordsworth is quoted, then turned round to describe a recess in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's line 'The child is father of the man' gives LAD + IS + PA; 'the reverse' turns the whole run backwards. 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church, and the adjective means shaped like or belonging to one.

clue.text: Circular to abolish a right

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish

explanation.surface: A notice goes round announcing that a right is being taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ring-shaped is round, so circular and ring-shaped are synonyms.

clue.text: Change of neckwear for every week-day, now

definitions.text: Change of neckwear for every week-day

explanation.surface: A dapper man sports a fresh tie each day of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie for each of the seven days makes SEVEN TIES; 'now' is the decade in which the puzzle was printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A different necktie for each day of a week is seven ties; the decade from 1970 was the present when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Greek letter of deposit

explanation.surface: A Greek letter is asked about something put down or paid in.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet; a river's silt deposit at its mouth takes the same name from its triangular shape.

clue.text: A disorderly rascal, this sailor

indicators.note: disorderly means jumbled up, so the letters of rascal are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unruly rogue turns out to be a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia who served on European ships.

clue.text: An Indian trophy, the Spanish knife

parts.note: a scalp was taken as a trophy of war in old stories of Native Americans
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A war trophy and a Spanish blade are listed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small, very sharp cutting blade is this kind of knife.

clue.text: Talks maliciously of a river man around Leatherhead

indicators.note: around means the river man's name is wrapped about the other letter

parts.note: Sanders of the River is Edgar Wallace's colonial river officer
the head of the word leather is its first letter, L

explanation.surface: Someone spreads malicious gossip about a boatman near Leatherhead, a town in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a Surrey town, but here it is split as 'Leather head', its first letter L, put inside SANDERS. 'of a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander is to make false, damaging spoken statements about someone.

clue.text: Athenian sailor has such refined wit

parts.note: Attic means belonging to Athens or Attica
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A Greek seaman shows a polished sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant, delicate humour was the hallmark of Athenian writers, hence the phrase for refined wit.

clue.text: A king whose public relations are very /early in the morning?

parts.note: one in the morning, 1 am, written with I for one

explanation.surface: A monarch's publicity people work very early hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 AM is very early in the morning, with the figure 1 standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy during the Trojan War.

clue.text: Accompanying effects of Horner's activity ?

annotationWithheld.why: Accompanying effects of Horner's activity ? (7): 'Accompanying effects' defines LUGGAGE, but no reading of 'Horner's activity' giving the answer can be confirmed

clue.text: Middleman's orange

explanation.surface: A go-between is asked what fruit he prefers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' reads as the middle of a man: the belly button sits there.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button sits at the middle of the body, and a seedless orange with a button-like end shares the name.

clue.text: Very few fish on the beam

parts.note: scant means barely enough, very little
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Hardly any fish are caught by the light of a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A scantling is a timber of small cross-section, such as a rafter or joist.

clue.text: Assist by seconding a worker

parts.note: seconding a staff member means lending them to another post
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An employer helps out by transferring a member of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone with a task is a common idiom for assist.

clue.text: For one with a sentence it's a bit of a break

definitions.text: For one with a sentence it's a bit of a break

parts.words: For one with a sentence it's a bit of a break
parts.note: reads as a convict getting time off, but means the punctuation mark that makes a short pause inside a written sentence

explanation.surface: A prisoner serving time is given a small respite.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark marks a slight pause, a small break, within a sentence.

clue.text: Rules-—for horse-control, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for horse-control is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: reins are the straps a rider uses to steer a horse

explanation.surface: Rules are laid down for controlling a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch reigns, that is rules over a country, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: He supplies our daily needs

parts.note: reads as a grocer or provider of essentials, but a daily is a newspaper delivered or sold every day

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper provides our everyday essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper, and the shopkeeper who sells papers supplies them.

clue.text: Making for a terrible vice rate

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of vice and rate are in a bad state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is heading for an appalling level of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' links. The definition works as in 'the making of art': creative and making both describe bringing something into being.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative work is the act of producing or inventing, so it describes making things.

clue.text: Self-styled paragon is tense

explanation.surface: Someone who thinks themselves perfect is wound up and nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is what a self-styled paragon says: I'M PERFECT. 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster claims to be flawless; the grammatical tense for continuing past action, as in 'was walking', has the same name.

clue.text: Ready 40 give a soft red outside trim

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

indicators.note: outside means red is placed around the word for trim

parts.note: to pare is to trim by cutting away the edge

explanation.surface: Someone is set to hand over a gently red decoration for the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give a' links; 'red' looks like a colour for the trim but is a container wrapped around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set and equipped in advance is to be ready.

clue.text: The Minstrel Boy's Open Sesame ?

parts.note: Open Sesame is the magic phrase that opens the robbers' cave; the Minstrel Boy of the song goes off to war, where a sentry demands a secret phrase to let a soldier by

explanation.surface: An old song's young musician knows the magic phrase for getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Minstrel Boy' is an Irish song: 'The minstrel boy to the war is gone'. A soldier passing a sentry needs the secret word.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word spoken to be allowed through a guarded point acts like a magic opening phrase.

clue.text: You trample on his work

parts.note: sounds like contempt for someone's efforts, but his work is the paving you walk over

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their labours are treated with disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: A paviour lays paving stones, which people walk over every day.

clue.text: Gilbert's limited company

parts.note: points to a firm, but means the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera about an ideal island turned into a limited company

explanation.surface: A man named Gilbert runs a small business.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's opera is 'Utopia, Limited' (1893), in which a South Sea kingdom becomes a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal imaginary state names the operetta 'Utopia, Limited', whose island is floated as a limited company.

clue.text: Swear crudely about points in the replies

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the points
crudely means roughly put together, so the letters of swear are rearranged

parts.note: N and S are two compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: Someone curses coarsely about the details in the responses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crudely' makes AWERS from SWEAR; 'about' puts it around N and S. 'in the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses to questions are replies, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Rush madly to make progress in life

explanation.surface: Dashing about wildly in order to get ahead in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge along at speed is one sense of the verb; a person's working life and advancement is the noun sense.

clue.text: Maybe half astonished by this residence

definitions.text: Maybe half astonished by this residence

parts.words: Maybe half astonished by this residence
parts.note: astonished can be split as Aston-ished: Aston is half of the football club name, and this house supplies the other half

explanation.surface: A visitor is somewhat amazed by a grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'Aston' is one half of the name, and a grand country house gives the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country or suburban house is a villa, and the word completes the club name.

clue.text: Not upright in speech

parts.note: upright can mean vertical or honest, so this describes being flat on the ground and also telling untruths

explanation.surface: A speaker is dishonest in what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horizontal and telling falsehoods share one word, matching both senses of not upright.

clue.text: Panty programmes hold up the speakers

explanation.surface: A political party's policies support those who address the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's stated set of policies is its manifesto; raised stages support people giving speeches.

clue.text: Something cold from the holy man

parts.note: fro is an old form of from, kept in 'to and fro'
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: Something chilly comes from a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice crystals forming on surfaces in freezing weather are a cold thing.

clue.text: Green actor found in the grove

parts.note: olive is a shade of green
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A green performer is discovered among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a leading London actor around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive groves are planted with these, so the plant is what is found in such a grove.

clue.text: Order direction like Caesar's entourage ?

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
SE, south-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An honour is ordered for the followers of a Roman leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare, Caesar says 'Let me have men about me that are fat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Caesar wants men about him who are fat, so his ideal followers are very overweight.

clue.text: The grid may be put in order

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of the grid could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword grid can be tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting something upright or straight again is to put it in order.

clue.text: Turns to tears, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of to tears are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is reduced to crying by bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning round on an axis is what something that turns does.
